newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African wool prices ease at latest auction.
newsitem.headline: S.African wool prices ease at latest auction.

text.p: South African wool prices eased marginally at the latest auction, but held up well in the face of the depressed Australian wool market.
1,914 bales were offered at this week's sale, of which 96.5 percent was sold.

There were no price quotes for long Merino fleeces of 19 micron. But prices for long Merino fleeces of 20 micron fell 1.6 percent from the previous sale, 21 micron slipped 1.4 percent, 22 micron shed 3.3 percent, 23 micron down 2.3 percent, 24 micron cut 3.0 percent, 25 micron off 0.1 and 26 micron fell 1.1 percent.
Prices for Merino bellies rose 0.2 percent, Merino lambs fell 2.2 percent, Merino locks cut 5.2 percent, other white wools slid 1.3 percent.
The wool board said market analysts were of the opinion that, with the exception of fine wool, no significant price changes would occur in the near future.
It was however expected that the market would firm towards the second half of the season and enter an upward trend.
Next sale will be on September 18, offering 10,000 bales.
